movement_source: row 'Net interest margin (%)', column Full Year Ended 30 Jun 25 -> column Full Year Ended 30 Jun 26
headline: CBA's Group net interest margin fell 3bps to 2.05% in FY26 from 2.08% in FY25 (ev-9, ev-18, ev-41). Net interest income still rose $1,563m or 7% to $25,586m as average interest earning assets grew 8% (ev-16, ev-11). The bank frames the decline as essentially technical: "Margins were broadly stable excluding growth in liquid assets and institutional reverse sale and repurchase agreements, which have broadly neutral impacts on net interest income" (ev-39, ev-11, ev-42). The results book walk (primary framing) is: Liquids -3, Asset pricing -5, Funding costs 0, Portfolio mix +2, Basis risk 0, Capital/Replicating/Other +5, Treasury & Markets -2 (ev-1). So competition-driven lending margin compression (-5bps, mostly home loans -4bps) and liquids drag (-3bps) were largely offset by hedge/replicating earnings (+5bps) and favourable asset and funding mix (+2bps). The slide deck publishes the same 208→205 walk with a different cut of two bars (Liquids & repos -4, Treasury & Markets -1) — a definitional grouping difference, not a different total (ev-21).

drivers.columns: Jun 26 Full Year vs Jun 25 Full Year
drivers.narrative: Largest single drag after pricing. Liquid asset average balances rose $15 billion or 9% to $187 billion (ev-17); the bank stresses liquids growth has "broadly neutral impacts on net interest income" and margin was "stable" excluding it (ev-11, ev-39). Sensitivity: every $10bn of liquids cuts Group NIM ~2bpts (ev-36).

drivers.columns: Jun 26 Full Year vs Jun 25 Full Year
drivers.narrative: "Decreased margin by 5 basis points driven by home lending pricing (down 4 basis points) and business and institutional lending pricing (down 1 basis point), primarily reflecting the impact of competition" (ev-12). The slide splits it further: home loan competition -3, cash rate lag -1, Business & Insto. lending -1 (ev-26, ev-27, ev-28).

drivers.columns: Jun 26 Full Year vs Jun 25 Full Year
drivers.narrative: The bank publishes a zero bar and states "Funding costs: Flat." for the full year (ev-13, ev-4) — an explicit statement that deposit and wholesale funding pricing contributed nothing net over FY25. No reason is disclosed for the full-year offset; deposit growth is credited under portfolio mix instead. Corroborated at 0 on the slide walk (ev-21).

drivers.columns: Jun 26 Full Year vs Jun 25 Full Year
drivers.narrative: "Increased margin by 2 basis points driven by favourable asset mix from strong growth in business lending and favourable funding mix from strong growth in deposits" (ev-14). The slide labels it "Favourable asset mix and deposits growing faster than lending" (ev-34). Business and corporate average balances grew 10%; deposit funding ratio 79% (ev-14, ev-34).

drivers.columns: Jun 26 Full Year vs Jun 25 Full Year
drivers.narrative: Published as a zero bar; the book states "Basis risk: Flat." (ev-15, ev-6). Context on the exposure: "Jun 26 average BBSW/OIS spread = 6bpts" and every 7bpts of spread is ~1bpt of Group NIM (ev-37). The slide walk does not print a separate basis risk bar (ev-21).

drivers.columns: Jun 26 Full Year vs Jun 25 Full Year
drivers.narrative: The largest positive: "Increased margin by 5 basis points driven by higher earnings on the replicating portfolio due to changes in portfolio rate and volume (up 4 basis points) and higher earnings on capital hedges (up 1 basis point)" (ev-19). Slide: "Interest rate risk hedging" +5, split replicating portfolio +4 and higher earnings on capital +1, as swap rates increased in FY26 (ev-30, ev-31, ev-35, ev-38).

drivers.columns: Jun 26 Full Year vs Jun 25 Full Year
drivers.narrative: "Decreased margin by 2 basis points due to lower risk management income in Treasury and growth in reverse sale and repurchase agreement balances" (ev-20). The repo element is margin-dilutive but broadly earnings-neutral (ev-39). The slide prints this bar as -1, grouping the institutional repo drag (-1) into Liquids & repos instead (ev-21, ev-24).

disagreements.topic: Grouping of liquids/repos vs Treasury & Markets bars in the NIM walk
values: Profit announcement p28: Liquids (3)bps, Treasury & Markets (2)bps
Presentation p60: Liquids & repos (4)bps, Treasury & Markets (1)bps
disagreements.preferred: Profit announcement p28: Liquids (3)bps, Treasury & Markets (2)bps
disagreements.explanation: Both walks run 208 to 205 and sum correctly. The slide moves the (1)bp institutional repo balance-growth drag out of Treasury & Markets and into a combined "Liquids & repos" bar; the results book leaves it in Treasury & Markets. Total movement is identical (-3bps); only the attribution boundary differs. Per source hierarchy the results book's framing is primary.

limitations: The bank qualifies the headline decline heavily: excluding growth in liquid assets and institutional reverse repos - which have 'broadly neutral impacts on net interest income' - it says margin was stable (ev-11, ev-39). On that basis the -3bps liquids bar (and the repo component of Treasury & Markets) does not reduce net interest income dollars, so the reported NIM fall overstates the economic margin pressure.

'Funding costs: Flat.' and 'Basis risk: Flat.' are published as zero bars with no explanation of what offset within them; the deposit/wholesale split inside funding costs is not disclosed for the full year. Deposit growth benefit is captured under Portfolio mix instead, so funding.deposits cannot be quantified separately.
The half-on-half walk (Dec 25 to Jun 26: Funding costs +2, Asset pricing -5, Capital/Replicating +3, Treasury & Markets +1) is a different comparison and was excluded from the driver table.
No CBA-published 'NIM excluding liquids and pooled facilities' numeric level was found; the 'broadly stable' claim is narrative only, not a quantified alternative margin.
